==Problem==

Define a sequence recursively by <math>F_{0}=0,~F_{1}=1,</math> and <math>F_{n}=</math> the remainder when <math>F_{n-1}+F_{n-2}</math> is divided by <math>3,</math> for all <math>n\geq 2.</math> Thus the sequence starts <math>0,1,1,2,0,2,\ldots</math> What is <math>F_{2017}+F_{2018}+F_{2019}+F_{2020}+F_{2021}+F_{2022}+F_{2023}+F_{2024}?</math>

<math>\textbf{(A)}\ 6\qquad\textbf{(B)}\ 7\qquad\textbf{(C)}\ 8\qquad\textbf{(D)}\ 9\qquad\textbf{(E)}\ 10</math>

==Solution==

A pattern starts to emerge as the function is continued. Note that each next term in the sequence is the sum of the previous two terms mod 3. The repeating pattern of 8 terms is <imath>0,1,1,2,0,2,2,1\ldots</imath> The problem asks for the sum of eight consecutive terms in the sequence, starting from the 2017th. Since the pattern repeats in cycles of 8, we divide 2017 by 8 and we find that the 2017th term is the same as the remainder, the first term. Thus the sum of the sequence from the 2017th to the 2024th term is the same as the sum of the first eight terms. We now just need to find the sum of the first eight numbers, which is just the same as the cycle noted above. Doing this, we get <imath>\boxed{\textbf{(D)}\ 9}</imath>
